title: Quiz: Lean Six Sigma — Waste Elimination and Quality Tools

questions.text: A data team generates a daily summary report that is never read by anyone. Which Lean waste category is this?
questions.explanation: Producing output that is not needed or used is Overproduction — one of the 8 Lean wastes. Resources are consumed without delivering value.

questions.text: Process Cycle Efficiency (PCE) is calculated as:
questions.explanation: PCE = Value-adding time / Total lead time × 100%. A Lean target is typically > 25% PCE; most traditional processes run at 5–15%.

questions.text: Poka-Yoke (mistake-proofing) is designed to make it impossible or very difficult to create a defect, rather than detecting defects after they occur.
questions.explanation: Poka-Yoke is a preventive Lean tool — it designs the process so errors cannot be made (e.g., a USB plug that only fits one way). This is more effective than inspection-based defect detection.

questions.text: In a Big Data pipeline, data records sitting idle in a landing zone for 4 hours waiting for a scheduled batch job is an example of which Lean waste?
questions.explanation: Idle data waiting to be processed is the data equivalent of Inventory waste — work in progress that has been started but is not yet complete, consuming storage and delaying value delivery.

questions.text: Lean Six Sigma combines Lean's focus on speed and waste elimination with Six Sigma's focus on variation reduction and defect elimination.
questions.explanation: Lean Six Sigma integrates both approaches: Lean tools (VSM, 5S, Kanban) eliminate waste and improve flow, while Six Sigma tools (control charts, DMAIC, DOE) reduce variation and defects.
